topics.name: Develop an appreciation and love of reading, reading increasingly challenging material independently (wide range of fiction and non-fiction including whole books, short stories, poems and plays; high-quality pre-1914 and contemporary English literature; Shakespeare; seminal world literature)
Choose and read books independently for challenge, interest and enjoyment
Reread books encountered earlier to increase familiarity and provide a basis for comparison
Understand increasingly challenging texts: learn new vocabulary using context and dictionaries
Make inferences and refer to evidence in the text
Know the purpose, audience for and context of writing and draw on this to support comprehension
Check understanding to make sure what has been read makes sense
Read critically: know how language, vocabulary, grammar, text structure and organisational features present meaning
Recognise a range of poetic conventions and understand how these are used
Study setting, plot and characterisation, and their effects
Understand how dramatists' work is communicated through performance and how alternative staging allows different interpretations
Make critical comparisons across texts and study a range of authors, including at least 2 authors in depth each year
Write accurately, fluently, effectively and at length for a wide range of purposes and audiences (formal essays, narrative, stories, scripts, poetry, talks, arguments, personal and formal letters)
Summarise and organise material, supporting ideas and arguments with necessary factual detail
Apply growing knowledge of vocabulary, grammar and text structure, selecting the appropriate form
Draw on knowledge of literary and rhetorical devices from reading and listening to enhance impact
Plan, draft, edit and proofread, considering how writing reflects audience and purpose
Amend vocabulary, grammar and structure to improve coherence and effectiveness
Pay attention to accurate grammar, punctuation and spelling, applying KS1/2 spelling patterns and rules
Extend and apply grammatical knowledge (KS1/2 appendix 2) to analyse more challenging texts
Study the effectiveness and impact of the grammatical features of texts read
Draw on new vocabulary and grammatical constructions from reading and listening, using them consciously for effect
Know and understand differences between spoken and written language, formal/informal registers, and Standard English and other varieties
Use Standard English confidently in own writing and speech
Discuss reading, writing and spoken language with precise and confident use of linguistic and literary terminology
Use Standard English confidently in a range of formal and informal contexts, including classroom discussion
Give short speeches and presentations, expressing ideas and keeping to the point
Participate in formal debates and structured discussions, summarising and building on what has been said
Improvise, rehearse and perform play scripts and poetry, using role, intonation, tone, volume, mood, silence, stillness and action to add impact
